title: SAEP-02
body:
Originating forum post: https://forum.sky.money/t/saep-02-modify-spark-liquidity-layer-core-relayer-and-freezer-multisig-configuration/27318

**Do not merge unless associated poll passes**
author: blimpa
summary: Summary This proposal is submitted by Phoenix Labs in its role as a nested contributor (as defined in Spark Artifact A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.1.1). It recommends edits to the Spark Artifact to (i) grant the Spark Assets Foundation (SAF) formal, operational access to the Spark Liquidity Layer (SLL) via the Core Operator Relayer Multisig, and (ii) improve incident response for the SLL by updating the Freezer Multisig threshold and signers. Specifically: Add SAF as a co-controller of the Core Operator Relayer Multisig alongside Amatsu and set the threshold to 2/5 with signers distributed across Amatsu, SAF, and Phoenix Labs (PL). Reduce the Freezer Multisig threshold from 2/4 to 1/4 and update signers to enable faster freezes in emergencies. These changes align with SAF’s mandate in A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4.3 – Spark Assets Foundation and update the following artifact sections: A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.2 – Core Operator Relayer Multisig (CORE) A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.2.2 – Required Number of Signers (CORE) A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3 – Freezer Multisig (CORE) A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3.2 – Required Number of Signers (CORE) A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3.3 – Signers (CORE) Background The SLL relies on tightly scoped relayer roles to perform operational actions and on a dedicated FREEZER_ROLE to halt activity across relayers in emergencies. Under the current artifact, the Core Operator Relayer Multisig holds RELAYER_ROLE authority (A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.2.1.1.2 – Relayer Role) and is controlled by Amatsu. As the ecosystem evolves, SAF’s legal and operational remit (A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4.3 – Spark Assets Foundation) requires direct, controlled access to execute SLL operations consistent with asset stewardship. Separately, security reviews have highlighted that, for high-severity incidents freeze latency is a critical risk factor. Reducing the Freezer Multisig threshold improves time-to-freeze, and decreases the risk of the system. Proposal Details Core Operator Relayer Multisig (RELAYER_ROLE) Add SAF as a co-controller alongside Amatsu. Set threshold to 2/5 with the following signer allocation: 2 Amatsu signers 2 SAF signers 1 Phoenix Labs signer (PL) Rationale: Ensures SAF can fulfill its asset oversight mandate while maintaining shared control and separation of duties. PL’s single signer improves proposal flow and operational throughput without concentrating approval power. Freezer Multisig (FREEZER_ROLE) Reduce threshold from 2/4 to 1/4. Update signers to: 1 SAF signer 2 Phoenix Labs signers VoteWizard Rationale: In emergencies, speed quorum size; a 1/4 threshold materially lowers response time. Risk of an erroneous freeze is considered less impactful than delayed freezing and is mitigated by clear unfreeze paths and post-incident review. Specification Option 1: For Adopt the following Spark Artifact changes. Edits — Core Operator Relayer Multisig A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.2 – Core Operator Relayer Multisig (CORE) Current: “The Core Operator Relayer Multisig has the RELAYER_ROLE … and is controlled by Amatsu.” Replace with: “The Core Operator Relayer Multisig has the RELAYER_ROLE as defined in A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.2.1.1.2 – Relayer Role and is jointly controlled by Amatsu and the Spark Assets Foundation in accordance with A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4.3 – Spark Assets Foundation.” A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.2.2 – Required Number of Signers (CORE) Current: “2/3 signing requirement.” Replace with: “2/5 signing requirement.” (New/clarified) A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.2.3 – Signers (CORE) Set to: “The Core Operator Relayer Multisig comprises the following signers: • Amatsu: 2 signers • Spark Assets Foundation (SAF): 2 signers • Phoenix Labs (PL): 1 signer Phoenix Labs’ signer may create and propose transactions; execution requires meeting the 2/5 threshold.” Edits — Freezer Multisig A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3 – Freezer Multisig (CORE) Current: The Freezer Multisig has the FREEZER_ROLE as defined in A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.2.1.1.4 - Freezer Role and is controlled by the Governance Facilitators. Replace with: The Freezer Multisig has the FREEZER_ROLE as defined in A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.2.1.1.4 - Freezer Role and is controlled by Spark Assets Foundation, Phoenix Labs and Votewizard. A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3.2 – Required Number of Signers (CORE) Current: “The Freezer Multisig currently has a 2/4 signing requirement.” Replace with: “The Freezer Multisig has a 1/4 signing requirement.” A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3.3 – Signers (CORE) Current: “VoteWizard, JanSky, LDR, CivicSage.” Replace with: “The Freezer Multisig has the following signers: • Spark Assets Foundation (SAF): 1 signer • Phoenix Labs (PL): 2 signers • VoteWizard: 1 signer” Non-functional / Process Notes Operational Scope: These changes grant SAF operational access commensurate with its already approved role. Option 2: Against Reject the above proposal. Make no changes to the Spark Artifact. Justification Mandate Alignment: SAF must be able to exercise its asset oversight responsibilities (A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4.3). Adding SAF signers and co-control to the Core Operator Relayer is the minimal viable change to reflect this mandate. Separation of Duties Safety: A 2/5 threshold across three independent entities (Amatsu, SAF, PL) preserves decentralization while allowing efficient execution. Incident Response: For high-severity threats, freeze time is critical. Moving the Freezer Multisig to 1/4 materially reduces the time to freeze. The downside risk of a mistaken freeze is bounded and reversible; the downside risk of a delayed freeze is deemed greater. Operational Efficiency: Allowing PL to propose Core Operator transactions improves throughput while preserving SAF/Amatsu execution control. Governance Process Review: Spark Risk Council and Operational Facilitator to review within 7 days of forum submission. Scheduling: If cleared, included in Spark’s next available weekly governance cycle (beginning on the Monday following the next Friday 08:00 UTC after clearance). Voting: Simple majority, 3-day voting period. Phoenix Labs submits this proposal as a nested contributor per A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.1.1. Conflicts No material conflicts to disclose.
